title: OPUSPOPULI Users
description:
Signup, activation and retention, read straight from Postgres.

Prometheus carries no auth or user metrics — MetricsService has no signup or login counters — so these panels query the database rather than the metrics store. That also means full history from the first account rather than from whenever a counter shipped.

PRIVACY: aggregates only. No panel selects email, name, IP address or street address, and geography stops at state. The datasource is expected to be a READ-ONLY role — see docs/guides/user-dashboard.md.

panels.title: Total users
panels.description: Accounts that exist right now. Soft-deleted accounts are excluded — deleted_at IS NULL is the definition of an account everywhere else in the codebase, and a dashboard that counted them would drift from every other number we quote.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "total"
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

panels.title: New in last 7 days
panels.description: Independent of the dashboard time range on purpose: this is the number you want when someone asks 'how is signup going' regardless of what the picker is set to.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "new"
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
  AND created > now() - interval '7 days'

panels.title: Active in last 24h
panels.description: Distinct users with session activity in the last 24h. Approximate: user_sessions stores only the most recent activity per session, so a user active yesterday and today counts once, on today.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(DISTINCT user_id) AS "active"
FROM user_sessions
WHERE revoked_at IS NULL
  AND last_activity_at > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: Returning users
panels.description: Accounts that have logged in more than once. The single most useful early signal that the product is worth coming back to — a signup is a promise, a second login is evidence.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "2+ logins"
FROM user_logins l
JOIN users u ON u.id = l.user_id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND l.login_count >= 2

panels.title: Accounts locked now
panels.description: Lockouts in force. A rising number here is either an attack or a broken login flow, and both want looking at today rather than in the weekly review.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS "locked"
FROM user_logins l
JOIN users u ON u.id = l.user_id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND l.locked_until > now()

panels.title: Commitments acknowledged
panels.description: Share of accounts that have acknowledged the public ethical commitments (#754). Falling below 100% means people are getting past onboarding without the step firing.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(
         100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE commitments_acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL)
         / nullif(count(*), 0)
       , 1) AS "percent"
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

SELECT
  date_trunc('day', created) AS time,
  count(*) AS "signups"
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(created)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Cumulative users
panels.description: Cumulative WITHIN the selected range — it starts from zero at the range start, so it is a growth shape, not an all-time total. 'Total users' above is the all-time number.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('day', created) AS time,
  sum(count(*)) OVER (ORDER BY date_trunc('day', created)) AS "total"
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(created)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Onboarding funnel
panels.description: Where people stop. Address-geocoded is the step worth watching: an address that never geocodes yields no jurisdictions, and a user with no jurisdictions sees a generic product.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'signed up' AS stage, count(*)::int AS users
FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'acknowledged commitments', count(*)::int
FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND commitments_acknowledged_at IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'added an address', count(DISTINCT u.id)::int
FROM users u JOIN user_addresses a ON a.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'address geocoded', count(DISTINCT u.id)::int
FROM users u JOIN user_addresses a ON a.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL AND a.geocoded_at IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'scanned something', count(DISTINCT d.user_id)::int
FROM documents d JOIN users u ON u.id = d.user_id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL

panels.title: How people sign in
panels.description: Passkey vs magic link. Drives where auth effort goes next.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(auth_strategy, 'unrecorded') AS metric, count(*) AS value
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Users by state
panels.description: State only, never city. A state-level count of a civic product is a rollout metric; a city-level one starts to describe individuals, which an ops dashboard has no business doing.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT a.state AS metric, count(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS value
FROM user_addresses a
JOIN users u ON u.id = a.user_id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND a.is_primary
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Daily active users
panels.description: Approximate, and understates the past: user_sessions keeps only the latest activity per session, so a long-lived session contributes one point on its most recent day rather than one per day it was used. Trend is meaningful; absolute history is not.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('day', last_activity_at) AS time,
  count(DISTINCT user_id) AS "active users"
FROM user_sessions
WHERE last_activity_at IS NOT NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(last_activity_at)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Signups by week and method
panels.description: Aggregates only. No dashboard panel selects email, name, IP address or street address — see the header note.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_char(date_trunc('week', created), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "week of",
  coalesce(auth_strategy, 'unrecorded') AS "method",
  count(*) AS "signups"
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(created)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, 3 DESC
